_deal: The board's test node, until he plays it.
author: jessica
source: his 2026-11-12 'yeah start' and 'keep going' (one of every type by the 19th): the first real mission on hailing (OT-9G, played and voiced 11-11)
_note: HAIL: a pilot whose navigation has died is circling over a planet, frightened. He hails the ship and talks him down.
THE PLAYER'S PART: the talk is the job. A frightened man needs one steady voice, and the closing line is the player telling him what to do.
One speaker: the pilot is both the call on approach and the ship he hails (a hailed ship speaks in the recipe speaker's voice). No give, ends or perk: the space build resolves none yet.

2026-11-12, Frances and Kieran (office/contractors/*/reviews/2026-11-12-delve-MB117a.md): both reworks were the sheet: it hid a ship talk's lines (fixed in delve_sheet); the first prompt is the steady instruction. Frances's pick, does the player steer him: NO, he steadies him, so 'talk him down' (a landing nobody stages) became 'calm him down' on the card, objective and record. The fuel clock is off the card (Kieran: no clock, and a scared man on a timer is a race). Kieran's pick: one path, the calming line first.

prose.name: Rescue: The Circling Pilot over <Planet>
prose.briefing: A pilot over <Planet> has lost his navigation and has been flying in circles for an hour. Someone needs to hail him and calm him down.
prose.card: A pilot over <Planet> lost his nav and won't stop circling. Hail him and calm him down.

broadcast: Anyone on this channel? My nav's gone and I've been going round in circles for an hour. If you can hear me, please hail me.
_speech: Charlie (ElevenLabs, unused in any Delve), young and frightened, relieved the moment someone answers. His ear decides.

beats.objective: Hail the circling pilot and calm him down
greeting: Oh, thank goodness, a real voice. My nav's dead, every reading says I'm somewhere I'm not, and I've stopped trusting my own eyes.

exchanges.prompt: Cut the engines. Breathe. Then read me your fuel.
reply: Cutting them. Breathing. Fuel's at a third, which is more than I thought. All right. I can do this now, I just needed someone else to say it.

exchanges.prompt: How long have you been out here?
reply: An hour, maybe two. I stopped looking at the clock when the clock started disagreeing with me.

beats.journal: A pilot over <Planet> had lost his navigation and was flying in circles. I hailed him and calmed him down.
